definition: A colloquial expression for connecting a screen, system, or environment to something like an API or server.
example: Hook up the real API instead of the mock data to check it.

definition: An expression meaning to remove code, settings, or dependencies that are no longer needed.
example: After validating the new feature, strip out the old branch code.

definition: An expression meaning to include a change in a deployment or automated flow and run it.
example: Put only the reviewed fixes through this deployment.

definition: An expression meaning to largely change an existing structure or implementation and rebuild it.
example: Since the scope is large, check whether partial fixes are possible before scrapping the whole thing.

definition: Work that improves the performance, quality, or usage scope of an existing feature or structure to a higher level.
example: We're enhancing the search accuracy and the response speed.

definition: Means clothing; in the field it is also used to refer to a company or business that plans, produces, and sells clothing.
example: The apparel company's merchandising team collaborates with the fabric vendor.

definition: A company that runs its own brand's direction, products, marketing, and sales.
example: The brand company sets the seasonal concept and the target price.

definition: A vendor that handles clothing development, material sourcing, and production on commission from a brand.
example: We commission the promotion vendor for everything from samples to main production.
note: This is the fashion production-outsourcing context. It differs from sales promotion in marketing.

definition: A method of producing and supplying products to the ordering company's requirements and brand.
example: This product is produced via OEM.

definition: A method where the manufacturer handles both product development and design and production and supplies it under the ordering company's brand.
example: Review the ODM vendor's development samples.

definition: A production vendor that sews cut fabric into garments.
example: Align the sewing specs and the delivery date with the sewing factory.

definition: A workspace or organization that makes trial garments according to patterns and specs before main production.
example: Deliver the revised pattern and fabric to the sample room.

definition: An organization or workspace that develops and revises patterns based on a garment's form and measurements.
example: Check the shoulder-line revision with the pattern room.

definition: A vendor that performs dyeing processes and related finishing on yarn, fabric, or products.
example: The dyeing factory runs tests for each color.

definition: A company that develops, produces, or distributes and supplies fabric.
example: Check the stock and the additional-production availability with the fabric vendor.

definition: An organization that manages the production schedule, quantity, processes, quality, and partner-factory progress.
example: The production management team checks the possibility of a delivery delay.

definition: An organization in charge of developing, selecting, quality-checking, and supplying the fabrics and materials used in products.
example: The materials team proposes fabrics suited to the season.

definition: A team that plans the product assortment, price, volume, and schedule in line with the market, sales, and brand direction.
example: Decide the quantity per style with the merchandising team.

definition: An organization that designs the seasonal concept and the garments, colors, and details.
example: The design room delivers the flat sketches and material combinations.

definition: Activities that inspect and manage whether products and the production process meet the set quality standards.
example: In QC before shipping, check the sewing and the measurements.

definition: An organization that manages the flow of goods: receiving, storage, movement, shipping, and delivery.
example: Share the inbound schedule with the logistics team before the event starts.

definition: A role that technically coordinates realizing the design intent into the actual garment's fit, measurements, and sewing specs.
example: The TD organizes the fitting comments and the measurement revisions.

definition: A person who makes garment production patterns according to the design and measurements.
example: Adjust the sleeve range of motion with the patternmaker.

definition: Material made by gathering fibers into a thin, long strand, used to make woven and knit fabrics.
example: The fabric's feel changes with the yarn's thickness and twist.

definition: The process of arranging and twisting short fibers into yarn.
example: Select raw material suited to the spinning conditions.

definition: The process of interlacing warp and weft to make woven fabric.
example: Changing the weave structure changes the surface feel.

definition: The process of making loops with yarn and connecting them to make knit fabric.
example: Check the stretch and thickness according to the knit structure.

definition: The threads laid in the lengthwise direction when weaving fabric.
example: Place the pattern based on the warp direction.

definition: The crosswise threads that interlace with the warp when weaving fabric.
example: Change the weft color to compare the fabric feel.

definition: The ratio of each fiber type that makes up a fabric or product.
example: Cross-check the fiber composition to be labeled against the test results.

definition: A value indicating the weight of fabric. GSM expresses weight per area as grams per square meter.
example: Even with the same structure, a higher weight can change how it wears.

definition: The crosswise width of fabric. The usable width for cutting is confirmed after excluding the selvage and such.
example: The fabric width changed, so recalculate the fabric consumption.

definition: The amount of fabric needed per product unit, such as one garment.
example: Calculate the fabric consumption by size and fabric width.

definition: The percentage by which fabric or product dimensions shrink before and after washing, processing, and so on.
example: Reflect the shrinkage rate in the pattern after checking it.

definition: A property indicating how well color holds up against external conditions such as friction, washing, and light.
example: For dark fabric, also check the rubbing colorfastness.

definition: A phenomenon where surface fibers tangle from friction and form small balls of fuzz.
example: Check the degree of pilling in the wear areas.

definition: A phenomenon where one material's color transfers onto another material it contacts.
example: Check whether color bleeding occurs on the light color blocks.

definition: A method of dyeing the yarn first and then making the fabric.
example: The check pattern is done with yarn dyeing.

definition: A method of dyeing after the fabric is made.
example: Piece-dye the same greige fabric by color.

definition: Fabric that has been woven or knit but not yet dyed or finished.
example: Check the greige stock and set the dyeing schedule.

definition: A finishing process that adjusts the feel, appearance, and shrinkage of fabric or garments through washing and treatment.
example: Compare the color and dimensions before and after washing.

definition: A term for a finishing that rotates or mechanically treats fabric or a product to adjust the feel or shrinkage stability.
example: Recheck the weight and width after tumbling.

definition: A finishing that spreads and fixes the fabric width while drying and heat-setting to adjust the width and form.
example: Check the target width and weight after stentering.

definition: A treatment that applies a substance to the fabric surface to give properties such as water resistance, feel, or appearance.
example: Check the condition of folded areas after coating.

definition: A finishing that bonds a film or another layer to fabric to make a multi-layer material.
example: Check the bonding condition after film lamination.

definition: A small trial-dyed sample made to match the target color before main dyeing.
example: Compare three lab dips against the standard color and approve.

definition: A trial-printed sample made before the main print run to check color, pattern, size, and quality.
example: Check the pattern size on the strike-off.

definition: The work of printing color and patterns onto set areas of fabric or garment surfaces.
example: Mark the print position and size on the flat sketch.

definition: A decorative method of stitching patterns or letters onto fabric or garments with thread.
example: Check the thread color and density of the logo embroidery.

definition: The work or stage of temporarily sewing a garment to check the form and fit while making revisions.
example: In the basted fitting, first check the shoulder and waist positions.

definition: A term for the first quantity produced or received.
example: We decide reorders based on the initial-run sales.

definition: The stage of producing the products to be sold at actual quantities based on the approved sample and specs.
example: We begin main production after the sample approval.

definition: A sample made before main production to confirm the actual materials, trims, and specs to be used.
example: Pass the PP sample approvals to the factory.
note: Sample stages, names, and approval processes can differ by brand and factory.

definition: A sample pulled from early main-production units to check the production quality and specs.
example: Check the label position and measurements on the TOP sample.
note: The sampling timing and required quantity should be confirmed with each buyer.

definition: A sample set made in multiple sizes to check the size grading and fit.
example: In the size set, also check the sleeve width of the small size.

definition: The work of arranging the cutting layout of pattern pieces, considering fabric usage and grain direction.
example: Adjust the marking to reduce fabric loss.

definition: The work of spreading and stacking multiple layers of fabric, aligned in length and direction for easy cutting.
example: Check the grain direction and tension during spreading.

definition: A material used to reinforce the form and body of garment parts such as collars and front plackets.
example: Choose an interlining strength suited to the thin fabric.

definition: Fabric added inside a garment to aid the feel, form, and finish.
example: Check that the lining length doesn't extend past the shell fabric.

definition: The fabric that forms the main outer surface of a garment.
example: Check the shrinkage difference between the shell and the lining.

definition: The unit of sewing or topstitch expression that the needle and thread make in the fabric.
example: Keep the visible stitch spacing consistent.

definition: Sewing that is visible on the outside to decorate or to fix the seam allowance and form.
example: Keep the topstitch width around the pocket consistent.

definition: A sewing method that wraps and stitches the fabric edge to prevent fraying or to join pieces.
example: Finish the seam allowance edges with overlock.

definition: A method of finishing a fabric edge by wrapping it with a strip of material.
example: Check that the neckline binding doesn't stretch out.

definition: Reinforcing a stress point with short, dense stitching.
example: Add a bartack at both ends of the pocket opening.

definition: A phenomenon where the area around a seam gathers or wrinkles due to fabric, thread, or tension.
example: Check the sewing conditions to reduce the side-seam puckering.

definition: A problem or product that doesn't meet the set specs or quality standards.
example: Record the defect types together with photos.

definition: The work of inspecting a product's measurements, sewing, stains, trims, and packaging against standards.
example: In the inspection before shipping, check for stains and loose threads.

definition: The work of checking, with equipment, whether metal foreign objects such as needle fragments remain in a product.
example: Record whether needle detection is complete in the shipping log.

definition: The work of arranging a garment's form, wrinkles, and surface using heat and pressure.
example: In pressing, keep the seams from showing through to the outside.

definition: A tag attached to a product that provides information such as brand, price, and item number.
example: Check that the hang tag's item number matches the actual product.

definition: A label that shows information needed to use the product, such as materials and washing and handling.
example: Check the care label wording against the final specs.

definition: When goods or materials arrive at a warehouse or store and their quantity and condition are checked.
example: Match the received quantity against the purchase order.

definition: Sending goods out of a warehouse or store for purposes such as orders or transfers.
example: Recheck the color and size before shipping.

definition: Dividing product quantities among stores, channels, or regions according to demand and plans.
example: Allocate the volume based on each store's sales pace.

definition: Restocking sold or short items to maintain appropriate inventory.
example: Quickly replenish the core sizes.

definition: A metric showing the share sold out of a period's received or available volume. The basis volume for the calculation is set by each organization.
example: Review additional orders based on the weekly sell-through rate.
note: It's used similarly to sales rate, but the denominator, period, and returns-handling basis can differ, so the metric's definition should be confirmed.

definition: A metric showing how much inventory cycled through sales over a period.
example: Review long-held products based on inventory turnover.

definition: Products or inventory that passed into the next period after a season or period ended.
example: Plan a separate sales channel for the carryover stock.

definition: Continuing to run a previous season's products or styles into the next season.
example: Carry over the basic shirt and add new colors.

definition: A distribution method of selling goods to businesses such as retailers in bulk or on set trade terms.
example: Send the next season's line sheet to the wholesale buyers.

definition: A distribution method of selling goods to the end consumer.
example: Distinguish the retail price from the wholesale supply price.

definition: A space displaying products so buyers and customers can view them and hold consultations or place orders.
example: Show the seasonal samples and materials in the showroom.

definition: An event that presents the next season's products and takes buyers' orders.
example: Prepare samples by size before the order fair.

definition: A temporary selling or experience space operated for a limited period.
example: Check the flow and stock before the pop-up opens.
note: This is the fashion-store context. It differs in meaning from a pop-up window on screen.

definition: Activities that convey the brand and sales message in a store through product, fixtures, lighting, and space staging.
example: Change the main fixture layout according to the VM guide.

definition: Furniture and devices that display or store products or make up the sales space.
example: Adjust the display to match the fixture height.

definition: A device for hanging garments to store or display them.
example: Arrange the color and size order on each rack.

definition: The state or combination of wearing garments and accessories together.
example: Organize the shots needed for each of one model's outfits.

definition: A photo showing a product actually being worn.
example: Please include front and back worn shots on the detail page.

definition: A state where a color difference appears between the same target color due to dye-lot or process-condition differences.
example: Check that there's no dye-lot color difference between the body and the sleeves.

definition: A state where the fabric grain or garment seams rotate or go crooked from the intended direction.
example: Check the side-seam skewing after washing.

definition: A state where a particular part of a garment doesn't sit naturally against the body or another part and lifts away.
example: Please fix the part where the back-neck collar gaps.
note: This entry is a fit issue where part of the garment lifts off the body when worn. Distinguish it from interlining bubbling, where fusible interlining separates from the shell fabric.

definition: A term for a state where fabric or seams aren't smooth and wrinkle like waves.
example: Please check the cause of the rippling around the zipper.

definition: A term for the width or ease of a garment's body section.
example: Keep the total length and just widen the body a little.

definition: The sensation—softness, resilience, roughness—felt when touching fabric by hand.
example: Check that the hand feel doesn't become too rough after washing.

definition: A term describing the form in which a garment or fabric falls along the body and gravity.
example: Revise it to a fit where the hem drapes naturally.

definition: A colloquial word used for various tasks such as making a sample, preparing quantity, or reducing measurements. What and how much must be confirmed from context.
example: Please pull one sample so we can see it at the fitting.

definition: A company that designs brands, visuals, products, and digital experiences on commission from clients.
example: Commission the brand revamp to the design agency.

definition: An organization or workspace that carries out design planning and production.
example: Review relevant work examples from the design studio.

definition: A team in charge of the design of products, brands, visuals, and experiences.
example: Align the screen layout priorities with the design team.

definition: A role that leads a team's or project's design direction and quality.
example: The design lead reviews the main user flows.

definition: A designer who designs a product's structure, experience, and screens considering user problems and business goals.
example: The product designer improves the sign-up flow.
note: Described in the digital product context. In industrial and product design, the same English title is also used for a role designing physical products.

definition: A role that designs the structure, flow, and interactions of the process by which a user accomplishes a goal.
example: The UX designer organizes the navigation flow.

definition: A role that designs the visual elements and interface expression of the screens a user operates.
example: The UI designer aligns the button states and spacing.

definition: A role that designs so a brand's identity is experienced consistently across many touchpoints.
example: The BX designer connects the tone of the packaging and the space.

definition: A designer who conveys messages visually through type, images, color, and composition.
example: The graphic designer creates the poster and leaflet.

definition: A designer who arranges the text and images of books, magazines, and brochures into readable pages.
example: The editorial designer lays out the body text and figures.

definition: A designer who designs movement for type, shapes, and images to convey a message and mood.
example: The motion designer produces the logo animation.

definition: A worker who expresses messages or scenes through drawing.
example: Commission the illustrator for the packaging artwork.
note: This means the person's role. Distinguish it from the Adobe Illustrator program of the same name.

definition: A role that researches user behavior, problems, and context to create the evidence needed for product and design decisions.
example: The UX researcher organizes recurring problems from the interviews.

definition: A role that designs on-screen guidance, buttons, and error messages so users can understand the product and act.
example: The UX writer refines the error messages to be easy to understand.

definition: The whole experience a user has while encountering and using a product or service.
example: Check the UX of the entire purchase process rather than a single screen.

definition: The whole experience a user has while encountering and using a product or service.
example: Review the purchase UX and the processing logic together so a duplicate request doesn't create two orders.

definition: The touchpoints—screens, inputs, outputs—through which a user sees and operates a system.
example: Adjust it so the UI reads even on small screens.

definition: The touchpoints—screens, inputs, outputs—through which a user sees and operates a system.
example: Handle it so the UI doesn't break even when the API response is empty.

definition: The work of designing classification, hierarchy, and navigation relationships so information is easy to find and understand.
example: Organize the IA first, then name the menus.

definition: The work of designing classification, hierarchy, and navigation relationships so information is easy to find and understand.
example: Build the screen routes and menu hierarchy according to the agreed IA.

definition: The path of screens and actions a user goes through to accomplish a goal.
example: Reduce unnecessary steps in the sign-up user flow.

definition: The path of screens and actions a user goes through to accomplish a goal.
example: Per the login user flow, implement it to return to the original page after authentication.
